The Chief of Field Office, UNICEF Kaduna, Dr Gerida Birukila, made the call on Friday during the 2026 World Children’s Day celebration held at Kaduna State Special Education School, with the theme, “My Day, My Rights, My Future.”
Birukila said children with disabilities were 50 per cent more likely to have never attended school and faced a higher risk of being excluded from primary education, according to UNICEF data .
She described the situation as a challenge to the global commitment to ensuring that every child enjoys the right to education, protection and inclusion, regardless of disability or background.
The UNICEF official urged the Kaduna State Government to establish more special education facilities and train a workforce capable of supporting children with different forms of disabilities.
She expressed particular concern about children in rural communities, noting that “even when parents were willing to enroll their children in school, the absence of appropriate facilities often prevented them from accessing education.
She further stressed the need for an inclusive curriculum that accommodates children with visual and hearing impairments, physical disabilities and other special learning needs.
According to her, Kaduna State Special Education School could serve as a model for other parts of Nigeria and Africa, adding that UNICEF would raise the need for additional support and the establishment of more branches to reach children across the country.
Responding to the appeal, the Kaduna State Commissioner for Education, Prof Abubakar Sani Sambo, who represented Governor Uba Sani, said he would communicate UNICEF’s recommendation for an increase in the number of special education schools to the governor.
Sambo also acknowledged the need to strengthen teacher training to ensure that educators in special schools possess the skills required to handle children with different disabilities.
He said he had directed the director of Planning in the Ministry of Education to take note of the recommendation for consideration in the ministry’s submissions to the governor.
The commissioner further recalled the constitutional provisions on employment opportunities for persons with disabilities, saying he would draw the governor’s attention to the need to create opportunities for children with disabilities to contribute to national development.
He reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to inclusive and equitable education under its SUSTAIN Agenda, including investments in school infrastructure, teacher development, learning materials and school safety.
